newsitem.title: USA: World Bank sees solid Argentine, Mexican recovery.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees solid Argentine, Mexican recovery.

text.p: Argentina and Mexico will post solid economic growth rates this year after bouncing back from the crisis of the Mexican peso, World Bank officials said on Monday.

Argentina's gross domestic product is expected to increase by five percent and Mexico's by between four and 4.4 percent, the bank's chief economist for Latin America, Guillermo Perry, said at a news conference.

"We are pretty confident that in the case of Argentina we are going to see growth rates of about five percent from this year onwards because the recovery is very balanced," said Perry, a former Colombian finance minister.
Argentina's GDP grew by 4.4 percent last year, after shrinking by 4.6 percent in 1995.

Perry noted that Argentina had strengthened its banking system, which had been buffeted by the so-called "tequila effect" of the peso crisis in late 1994 and early 1995 when a botched devaluation caused a run on the Mexican currency.
Domestic consumption in Mexico, however, will take longer to recover due to the effect of the 1995 recession, he said.
Mexico's growth rates would be dampened by the weight of corporate and personal debt run up during the 1994 credit boom prior to the crisis and its fallout on the banking sector.
"The (legacy) of the crisis is more profound in Mexico's case, so it's taking more time to work out the problems of indebtedness," he said.
Since consumer growth is only beginning to pick up and banks are just starting to resume lending, the World Bank's projections for Mexican growth are more cautious, Perry said.
Mexico's GDP grew by 5.1 percent in 1996, rebounding from a 6.2 percent drop in 1995.

The World Bank's Latin America and Caribbean department vicepresident, Shahid Javed Burki, said that the recoveries in Argentina and Mexico would help the whole region return this year to the growth rates attained before the peso crisis.
"The two countries that were badly hurt two years ago, Mexico and Argentina, have successfully weathered the storm and are now on their way to recovery," he said.
The recessions in the Argentine and Mexican economies dragged down the whole region's economic growth rate down to 1.3 percent in 1995, the lowest so far this decade.
